title: Bees and pollination
examples: What is the difference between nectar and pollen?
Can plants be pollinated without bees?

explain.say: Today we are learning about bees and how they help flowers.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the parts of a flower. Look at the petal, the sepal and the anther. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Flowers have parts that help them make seeds. Pollen is yellow dust on the flower.
Pollination happens when pollen moves from one flower to another flower.

items: Step 4: Pollen falls on Flower B

explain.say: Bees collect sweet liquid from flowers called nectar. This nectar is food for the bees.
Bees use nectar and pollen to make something sweet called honey. Honey is stored in the honeycomb.
Think about making a sandwich. You need bread, filling, and maybe some sauce.

faq.a: Bees collect nectar because it is a sugary liquid that gives them energy to live.
asks: What do bees drink from flowers?

faq.a: Pollen gets moved when bees brush against the flower parts while collecting food.
asks: Does the bee move the pollen?

faq.q: What is the main job of pollination?
faq.a: The main job of pollination is to help flowers make seeds so new plants can grow.
asks: What is the purpose of pollen?

faq.a: No, honey can taste different depending on the type of flowers the bees visit.
asks: Does flower type change honey taste?

faq.q: Do bees need flowers to survive?
faq.a: Yes, bees need flowers because flowers provide the nectar and pollen they need to eat.

facts: Pollen is the fine, yellow powder found in the male parts of flowers.
Bees collect nectar, which is a sugary liquid produced by flowers.
Pollination is the process of moving pollen from one flower to another.
Bees use nectar and pollen to create honey in their honeycomb.

quiz.say: Pollen moves from one flower to another by:

options.show: The flower blowing the pollen out.
options.say: The flower blowing the pollen out.

options.show: A bee landing on the flower.
options.say: A bee landing on the flower.

options.show: The wind blowing the pollen away.
options.say: The wind blowing the pollen away.

options.show: The rain washing the pollen off.
options.say: The rain washing the pollen off.

quiz.why: The bee acts like a carrier, moving pollen dust from flower to flower.

wrong.0: Flowers usually need help from animals to move pollen.
wrong.2: Wind can help, but bees are much better at moving it.
wrong.3: Rain usually washes pollen away, stopping pollination.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of pollination?

options.show: Make seeds so new plants can grow.
options.say: Make seeds so new plants can grow.

options.show: Attract more bees to the area.
options.say: Attract more bees to the area.

quiz.why: Seeds are what allow plants to reproduce and spread to new places.

wrong.1: Petals make them look colourful, but that is not the main job.
wrong.2: Nectar is sweet, but pollination is about making seeds.
wrong.3: Attracting bees is a result, not the main goal of pollination.

quiz.say: Bees store their food in a structure called:
quiz.why: The honeycomb is the specific wax structure bees build to store honey.

wrong.0: Nectar is the liquid food, but it needs to be processed and stored.
wrong.2: Bees carry pollen on their bodies, but they store food elsewhere.
wrong.3: The flower makes the food, but the bees store it in their home.
